extracted.intended_audience: local journalists, news editors, audience/engagement staff and news entrepreneurs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for local newsrooms and independent publishers on experiments and practices to reach, serve, and build trust with community audiences. Covers community listening, formats, staffing/paid ambassadors, integration into newsroom strategy, and sustainability considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concretely useful to the community
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism must be rooted in being concretely useful to the communities it serves, and act like a part of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sourcing and distributing cloth masks, producing a pamphlet listing local food pantries and benefits, improving poorly formatted school fliers. The Jersey Bee frames its mission to 'improve quality of life' and treat information needs like an essential service (compared to a public utility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Build power for communities and repair harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should aim to build power for community members and acknowledge and work to repair 'the harms of journalism and other institutions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bee's mission centers on serving BIPOC and working-class communities and addressing media redlining; reporting choices are shaped by how the outlet can help communities gain access and agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an information hierarchy of needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize issues essential to survival (food access, shelter) as the foundation for other reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic priorities should start with immediate civic/information needs before broader civic participation or policy coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do listening legwork before reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Earn community trust by doing listening work first, which empowers audiences to share ideas about what they want covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listening sessions, interviews, and in-person outreach create a stronger foundation for journalism and help identify impactful coverage priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed community engagement into core work
rubrics_metrics.description: Community engagement should be an integrated part of newsroom operations, not an occasional add-on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make community engagement repeatable and part of strategy so it reinforces reporting, fundraising, and product decisions rather than remaining isolated experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit and pay community ambassadors
rubrics_metrics.description: Hire community ambassadors who are networked with target communities (e.g., BIPOC, multilingual) and compensate them for outreach work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VTDigger example: five ambassadors paid $20/hour tasked with outreach, interviews, and weekly debriefs; ambassadors increased honesty and reach, and later served as vouching advocates for the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer value to communities before asking for something
rubrics_metrics.description: Give something to people or communities (services, advertising, resources) before extracting engagement or asking for participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VTDigger implemented 'Underwriting for Racial Equity'—offering free advertising to BIPOC businesses—as a way to give before asking for shares or engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mixed methods for community listening (surveys + interviews + in-person)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine online surveys, one-on-one interviews, and in-person outreach to get a fuller picture of community needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VTDigger's months-long project included 386 online surveys and 154 interviews; in-person work reached populations isolated from online news such as migrant dairy farmworkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach audiences where they are (platform and physical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about where your target audience congregates—both online (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube) and in physical spaces (galleries, community events)—and publish/engage there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art Rebellion prioritizes artists and experiments with Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, newsletters, and gallery/physical space partnerships to meet audiences on their platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish in multiple formats to increase reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Package projects in as many relevant forms as possible so they reach diverse segments of your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: newsletters, Instagram posts, YouTube videos, TikTok, and turning a reporting project into an art installation to reach artists and audiences who might not read traditional articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use unconventional storytelling formats when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider formats beyond straight reporting—music, rap, events, series that spotlight community members—to reflect community voices and build trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: La Converse supported youth to create a 'journalistic rap' and the 'Hood Heroes' series, which were shown at a forum on gun violence and led featured subjects to become ambassadors for the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat events and community gatherings as services first
rubrics_metrics.description: Design events to be a service to the community (the event is the service), with journalism as a secondary justification for writing about them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: La Converse's 'Dialogues' events create spaces for nuanced conversation on sensitive topics; the focus is service and building sustained engagement, not only content collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train community members and youth in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Build newsroom capacity and trust by training members of underrepresented communities to report and produce work about their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: École Converse trains young people in reporting and guides them through creating projects that reflect their lives and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay participants and contributors for their time
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensate people who provide information, fill out surveys, or contribute content to reduce extraction and increase equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art Rebellion pays artists $100 to complete its Artist Pay Project survey; paying increases participation and signals reciprocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt payment methods to participants' constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Use flexible payment mechanisms (Venmo, gift cards, etc.) to accommodate people without bank accounts or whose benefits could be jeopardized by certain payment forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VTDigger used Venmo and Visa gift cards for ambassadors who couldn't receive checks or lacked bank accounts; be creative to avoid excluding participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments as two parallel tests: audience impact and new workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: When trying new approaches, evaluate both whether the effort serves the audience and whether the newsroom can sustain the new way of working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label each new effort as an experiment in serving audiences and an experiment in workflow/process; this separation helps diagnose what worked and what didn't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make processes repeatable and document costs/metrices meticulously
rubrics_metrics.description: Create repeatable processes for experiments and track time/costs so the work can be evaluated, replicated, and funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document details like time to coordinate a postcard campaign; documented costs make future grant applications easier because you can propose proven processes with budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate experiments into overall newsroom strategy (activity systems maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use frameworks like Michael Porter’s activity systems maps to ensure new activities reinforce existing ones and to decide what to let go of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: LAist aligned voter guides, candidate interviews, and election results into an election strategy; experiments that don't immediately fit should be adapted or supported by partners to become sustainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use partnerships to lower implementation lift
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner with outside organizations (universities, funders) to reduce the resource burden of piloting new activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LAist used a university partner to pilot in-person workshops with lower lift; partnerships can make otherwise unaffordable experiments feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be present and show up without an agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustain trust by physically showing up to community events and protests without immediately reporting—listen and observe before publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term presence, not one-off surveys or meetings, is necessary for true community engagement; when you do publish, do so 'intentionally.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate projects by the extent to which they create ambassadors and feedback loops
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether projects produce community members who vouch for the outlet and suggest story ideas, indicating trust and ongoing engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambassadors and featured subjects becoming informal promoters (as with La Converse and VTDigger) is a sign of successful engagement and sustained reach.
